prompt.context: Our client is a cheese producer based in Vermont. Currently, they produce two types of cheese: Cheddar and Gouda. While revenues have grown, their profits have been decreasing. They have asked us to help them understand why and what they can do to increase profits.
prompt.question: Why have profits been decreasing despite growing revenues, and what can the client do to increase profits?

clarifying_info.q: Has the competitive landscape changed recently?
clarifying_info.a: The market is stable, with no major changes in competition in recent years.

clarifying_info.q: How does the client sell its cheese?
clarifying_info.a: They sell some cheese to wholesalers and a very small amount direct to consumer.

exhibits.title: Production Costs and Sales Data
exhibits.shows: A table showing per-unit production inputs (milk gallons, labor hours, energy kWh) for Cheddar and Gouda along with unit costs, aging time, warehouse details, and quarterly sales volumes and prices for Q4 2018 vs Q4 2019.

production_inputs.warehouse: 50,000 sq ft, $20,000/month rent; 1 lb = 1 sq ft while aging

framework: Revenue: analyze by product (Cheddar vs Gouda) — quantity sold per channel (wholesale vs direct-to-consumer) and price per channel
Costs — Variable: milk, labor, energy per pound for each product; Fixed: warehouse rent (tied to aging time and volume)
Market context: competitive dynamics, customer preference trends (organic, artisanal), channel shifts

questions.prompt: Calculate the variable cost per pound for Cheddar and Gouda.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply each input quantity by its unit cost for each product. Cheddar: milk $3.00, labor $0.24, energy $0.08. Gouda: milk $4.00, labor $0.40, energy $0.05.

math.setup: For each product, cost = (input qty) × (unit cost). Labor is per 100 lbs so divide by 100.
math.answer: Cheddar variable cost: $3.32/lb (milk+labor+energy). Gouda variable cost: $4.45/lb.

questions.prompt: Calculate the warehouse/aging cost per pound for each product.
questions.guidance: Aging time drives how long each pound occupies warehouse space. Cheddar ages 1 year = 12 months; Gouda ages 6 months. Monthly rent per sq ft = $20,000 / 50,000 sq ft = $0.40/sq ft/month. Cost per lb = $0.40 × months aged.

math.setup: Monthly rent per sq ft = total rent / warehouse size. Aging cost per lb = monthly rate × months aged.
steps: Monthly rent per sq ft: $20,000 / 50,000 = $0.40/sq ft/month
math.answer: Cheddar: $4.80/lb aging cost. Gouda: $2.40/lb aging cost.

questions.prompt: Calculate total cost, profit per pound, and total quarterly profit for Q4 2019. Has profit changed from Q4 2018?
questions.guidance: Total cost = variable costs + aging cost. Profit per lb = price − total cost. Total profit = profit per lb × lbs sold. Compare Q4 2018 to Q4 2019 total profit.

math.setup: Total cost per lb, then profit per lb, then multiply by Q4 2019 volumes. Repeat for Q4 2018 volumes to find the change.
math.answer: Total Q4 2019 profit = $11,925; Q4 2018 profit = $12,060; profit fell by $135. The decline is driven by lower Gouda volume (more profitable per lb) partially offset by higher Cheddar volume (less profitable per lb).

brainstorming.prompt: What can our client do to increase sales of Gouda cheese?

categories.name: Product
ideas: Sell a version aged only 3 months to reduce aging cost by $1.20/lb and offer a lower price point
Develop new Gouda varieties (smoked, herb-infused) to attract new customer segments
Improve packaging to signal premium/artisanal quality

categories.name: Place
ideas: Sell to high-end restaurants to increase brand awareness and command a premium
Expand to specialty food retailers and farmers markets
Pursue regional grocery chain distribution deals

categories.name: Promotion
ideas: Run in-store promotions and tastings at local grocery stores
Partner with food influencers or bloggers to raise awareness
Highlight Vermont provenance and artisanal credentials in marketing

categories.name: Price
ideas: Examine price elasticity to understand the effect of price changes on volume
Consider introductory pricing to trial new channels
Bundle Cheddar and Gouda for a combined price to boost Gouda pull-through

recommendation: Client should plan to increase sales of Gouda, which has a higher profit per pound ($1.14 vs $0.87), through increased brand awareness and better product positioning
Shifting volume mix toward Gouda will improve overall profitability even without changing prices or costs
risks: Increased marketing spend could reduce net profit if ROI is insufficient
Promotional pricing or a shorter-aged SKU could cannibalize premium positioning
Increased Gouda production may require more warehouse space or longer Cheddar aging to be deferred
Poor customer reception to new product variants is possible
next_steps: Hire an ad agency or run targeted promotions to boost Gouda brand awareness
Evaluate launching a 3-month aged Gouda SKU to capture a value-oriented segment
Run price elasticity tests to determine optimal Gouda pricing
Conduct a warehouse capacity analysis to ensure sufficient space if Gouda volume grows
